eva (ml): quick heads-up — ran HF chat_template -> Redwood conversion for model 'oasys-v1' and hit a weird edge. {% raw %} blocks are preserving Markdown code fences (```json ...) and Redwood's structured-output detector isn't picking up the JSON schema. example below.

sanjay (ml): hmm, raw is supposed to preserve literal text. do you have a minimal template and the rendered prompt?

eva (ml): minimal template we started from:
```jinja
{% raw %}
```json
{"intent": "{{ intent }}", "args": {{ args|tojson }} }
```
{% endraw %}
{{ system }}
{{ user }}
```

lin (infra): can you paste the final rendered prompt that we actually sent to the runtime (the one in the request body)? render-bot should have it in logs.

render-bot: rendered_prompt for ts=1713456789: 
"System: <system text>
User: <user text>
```json
{"intent": "order_food", "args": {\"items\": [\"sushi\"]}}
```"

marta (eng-evals): ok so the raw block preserved the triple-backticks, but our pre-send pipeline then HTML-encodes or escapes somewhere (we've seen ``` in other paths). Redwood's structured-output heuristic expects an unescaped code fence at the start of the assistant content or explicit sentinel. If fences are present but escaped or wrapped inside extra whitespace, the detector returns false -> we fall back to freeform text and downstream evals fail.

sanjay (ml): theory: HF chat_template->render step keeps fences, but our conversion layer that normalizes messages for the runtime calls html.escape() on template output. That kills the detector. repro: 1) raw block with fence -> 2) render -> 3) html.escape -> 4) send.

lin (infra): mitigation options:
- quick: strip HTML-escaping only for code-fence sequences before detection (risky)
- safer: convert fenced JSON in templates to a sentinel token at render time, e.g. <|json_start|> ... <|json_end|>, and teach structured-output detector to recognize sentinels too
- eval-run: add a post-render check in our bring-up harness that asserts detector(true) when template contains ```json

marta (eng-evals): for scheduled benchmarks this is bad — quant experiments expect strict JSON outputs for metric parsing. If we silently drop structured detection, eval scripts will break and we won't see quality regressions properly.

eva (ml): I'll open a small PR to (a) detect fenced-json blocks after rendering and replace fences with RW sentinels, (b) add unit test covering a Jinja {% raw %} fenced block. PR will also log if html-escape was applied so we can find other spots.

lin (infra): sounds good. Also add a quick e2e checklist: template -> render -> detector -> request body. If any step mutates the fences, fail the bring-up.

sanjay (ml): until the PR lands, workaround for teams: avoid relying on code fences in jinja raw blocks for structured outputs. instead add an explicit system line like: `System: You MUST return only JSON with keys: ...` That keeps evals alive.

marta (eng-evals): thanks — I'll update the evaluation harness to detect this class of mismatch and mark runs as 'conversion-warning' instead of silently misparsing.

eva (ml): pinging @lin for infra review and @sanjay for ML/heuristic sanity. cc @marta so evals can triage. :thumbsup:

lin (infra): noted, will review PR today. :eyes:

render-bot: added logfile entry: "render_escape_check=FAIL path=templates/order_flow.jinja reason=contains_fenced_json_after_escape"

sanjay (ml): nice, that log will help tracking. thanks all.
